status: Analysis plan fixed after previous results were viewed; exploratory, not preregistered confirmatory analysis
objective: C2 versus C3 difference in improvement magnitude
scope: practice; coreMtMs; C2 and C3; all available participants in those practice conditions
primary_pipeline: basic exclusion only: countedAsTrial=true and finite coreExitMs; no success exclusion; no statistical MT exclusion; no boundary exclusion
sensitivity_pipeline: same analysis, plus condition-by-original-trial-number MT mean +/- 1.5 sample SD exclusion, applied once after basic exclusion; rows shared across metrics

metrics.ER: core deviation rate in percent; differences in percentage points

aggregation: arithmetic mean of valid trial-row values within participant and block; equal participant weights; ER is unavailable if any included row has unknown ER

tests.improvement: 3 Welch tests of participant late-minus-early scores: MT, ER, TPe; primary scientific question
tests.early_late_performance: 6 Welch tests of participant means: each of MT, ER, TPe at early and late
tests.within_condition_change: 6 paired t tests, equivalent to two-time-point RMANOVA: each metric in each condition; report F=t^2
tests.slopes: 4 Welch tests: participant OLS slopes of trial-row metric against original trial number, separately early and late, for MT and TPe; units per trial
tests.within_person_variability: 2 Welch tests on log residual SD from participant late-block OLS fits, MT and TPe; residual SD uses residual degrees of freedom m-2; report geometric mean ratio
tests.between_person_variability: 4 median-centered Brown-Forsythe tests on participant late means and change scores, MT and TPe; no trial pooling
tests.profile: 3 balanced 2-condition x 4-block mixed ANOVA interaction tests, one per metric; always Greenhouse-Geisser correct using pooled within-condition covariance; no preliminary sphericity-test selection; measures temporal profile differences, not functional-family identity

multiplicity: 28 planned tests in primary pipeline adjusted jointly with Holm at alpha=0.05; same 28 sensitivity tests adjusted separately for descriptive robustness, never used to replace primary results; additionally provide Holm across all 56 as a reference
inference: nondirectional, two-sided mean contrasts; equal group variances not required for Welch; paired changes and mixed profile retain distribution assumptions; no test is selected according to observed p values
uncertainty: unadjusted 95% contrast CIs; primary-pipeline improvement additionally receives 95% BCa participant bootstrap CIs with 10000 resamples, batch 1000, seed 20261113+metric index; leave-one-participant-out effect range, without selection by p value
diagnostics: participant values, sample SD, skewness, ranges, zero counts, excluded row audit, unavailable metric audit, block counts, original input and analysis.py hashes; do not use normality tests to switch analysis methods
missing_policy: no imputation or silent participant removal; stop if any required participant-block estimate is unavailable, fewer than 3 valid OLS rows, zero residual SD, or nonfinite test statistic
resource_limit: one core and one BLAS thread; no nonlinear fitting or repeated model search; expected under one minute and below 500 MB
limitations: All results remain exploratory after prior analyses
Only 10 participants per condition; resampling does not remove small-sample uncertainty
ER proportion comparisons and mixed profile F tests are approximations
GG correction does not solve covariance heterogeneity across groups
No inference about long-term retention, transfer or asymptotic performance
No separate inferential test of ER individual variability because binary variance depends on ER
100-trial blocks respect rest boundaries but cannot separate rest effects from practice effects
The basic exclusion defines the target population of attempts and is not equivalent to all attempted trials
Sensitivity exclusion depends on participants jointly; inferential p values in that pipeline are descriptive
